findings.finding: qualification.qualifies_at_all_q -- the documented gate-12 primitive -- defaulted to enforce_gate_9=True, i.e. the peer-dependent gate 9 evaluated at every binding q, which is exactly the interpretation Authority Amendment 2 superseded. The production scan opted out explicitly, so the materialized cohort was correct, but the entrypoint was fail-OPEN: any other caller reached v1.4 semantics without asking for them.
findings.repair: Default changed to False (the amended per-candidate scope) and threaded into both the binding-q and diagnostic-q evaluations; the stale v1.4 docstring rewritten. Cohort byte-identity re-verified end to end by B.1.

findings.finding: test_cohort.py carried a module-level pytest.mark.skipif on the presence of the materialized cohort. Group A must have zero skips; had the artifact been absent, about thirty named group-A checks would have silently vanished from an A2 run while the receipt still read 'zero failures'.
findings.repair: A missing cohort now raises at collection time. It is a required A1 artifact, so its absence is a failure, never a skip.

findings.finding: The task graph names no A1 task owning the A3 storage preflight, the artifact-inventory stage-exit checker, the adjudication coverage checker, or the deadline plan selector and attrition branch -- yet B.7, B.8, B.10, B.11, B.12 and B.13 bind all four at A2.
findings.repair: Implemented as minimum complete frozen modules: storage_preflight.py, artifact_inventory.py, adjudication.py, deadline.py. The adjudication matrix is parsed from the hashed authority markdown rather than hand-copied, so it cannot drift.

findings.repair: Explicit cross-rung rule added; D.15 and D.25 assert it.

findings.finding: Four EXPECTED_ARTIFACT_INVENTORY.json rows are required_before_next_stage with a NULL missing_blocker (three B-GEN III-B provenance artifacts and the B-LOCK closure receipt). A null must not read as permission to exit the stage.
findings.repair: stage_exit_check fails closed under PROVENANCE_BINDING_MISSING for those rows; B.10 asserts both branches. No scientific value changes, so this is not an amendment trigger, but it is a defect in the inventory worth naming for the next authority pass.

findings.finding: The 75-vs-76 named-check discrepancy is internal to the HUMAN authority: section A2 says '12 group-B checks -- 75 named checks', while section 11 and the controlling test plan both say B = 13, total 76, and the plan enumerates B.1 through B.13. The machine authority carries no group counts, so there is no human/machine disagreement of the kind that triggers AUTHORITY_AMENDMENT_REQUIRED; the 75 line is a residual predating the v1.3 R2 repair that added B.13.
findings.repair: Resolved to 76 and recorded in this receipt.

findings.finding: EpisodeManager.buildArenaIfChanged and conditions.arena_cache_key compose the same fields in the same order with the same separator, but render floats differently (Java double toString vs Python repr). The authority requires the material to be part of the cache identity (C07), not byte equality across the seam, and the Python key is a receipt/spec artifact rather than the runtime key.

assert_claim_in_scope matches a claim to a row by substantive-token subset and refuses the never-established list plus each row's prohibited phrases. A claim that restates a permitted row AND appends an unlisted extra assertion would pass. No textual gate can close that.
findings.repair: The never-established list is the hard backstop; B.11 tests both directions.
